events.title: The first revelation
events.summary: Aisha's report places the beginning of revelation in the cave of Hira, following a period of meaningful dreams and seclusion.
events.uncertainty: The report supplies the setting; the CE year is conventional and approximate.

events.title: Khadija offers reassurance
events.summary: After the experience at Hira, Khadija reassured the Prophet ﷺ by recalling his care for relatives, guests, and people in difficulty.
events.uncertainty: A sequence within the first-revelation report, rather than a separately dated event.

events.title: A conversation with Waraqa
events.summary: Khadija brought the account to Waraqa ibn Nawfal, who connected the experience with earlier revelation and anticipated opposition.
events.uncertainty: The report describes the sequence without a calendar date.

events.title: Revelation after a pause
events.summary: Jabir's report describes revelation resuming after a pause and associates the moment with the opening instructions of Al-Muddaththir.
events.uncertainty: Exact length of the pause and CE date are not established here.

events.title: Calling the clans at Safa
events.summary: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet ﷺ gathered the clans at Safa and warned them publicly. Their answer acknowledged his previous truthfulness.
events.uncertainty: Commonly placed in the early public mission; the report itself gives no CE year.

events.title: Khabbab asks for help
events.summary: Khabbab recalled asking for help during persecution. The reported reply placed their suffering alongside the endurance of earlier believers.
events.uncertainty: A broad Makkan placement is used because this report does not date the exchange.

events.title: Abu Bakr and protection
events.summary: Aisha's report describes Ibn al-Daghina offering Abu Bakr protection, disputes about public worship, and Abu Bakr later releasing him from that agreement.
events.uncertainty: The episode predates the Hijrah, but the precise CE year is not supplied.

events.title: A difficult encounter and a merciful response
events.summary: When recalling a painful rejection, the Prophet ﷺ described declining an offer of destruction and hoping for future generations who would worship Allah.
events.uncertainty: Often associated with the Taif journey. The report names locations but gives no CE date.

events.title: The Night Journey and ascent
events.summary: The report of Malik ibn Sasaa describes the Night Journey and ascent, including the prescription of prayer.
events.uncertainty: The exact date is disputed. Its position here is a broad pre-Hijrah placement, not a fixed anniversary.

events.title: The pledges at Aqabah
events.summary: Ubada ibn al-Samit is identified as an Aqabah participant and reports a pledge covering worship and conduct.
events.uncertainty: This report identifies a participant and a pledge; it does not by itself establish every detail of the two Aqabah meetings.

events.title: The cave during the migration
events.summary: Abu Bakr recalls concern that pursuers might see them in the cave and the Prophet's reassurance. Quran 9:40 also refers to the two in the cave.
events.uncertainty: The Hijrah is conventionally dated to 622 CE. The report quoted here does not name the cave.

events.title: Suraqa on the route
events.summary: Suraqa's account describes pursuing the travelers, his horse stumbling, and his eventual request for a written assurance of safety.
events.uncertainty: The report supplies the episode; this schematic view does not reconstruct the exact route.

events.title: Arrival among Banu Amr ibn Awf
events.summary: Anas reports an initial stay among Banu Amr ibn Awf, followed by a welcome from Banu al-Najjar and arrival at Abu Ayyub's courtyard.
events.uncertainty: Relative sequence is clearer than an exact Gregorian day.

events.title: Building the mosque
events.summary: Anas describes preparing a site for the mosque in Madinah and the community's involvement in the work.
events.uncertainty: Shown after arrival. The cited report is the evidence for the construction episode.

events.title: Brotherhood and a market
events.summary: The report pairs Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf with Sad ibn al-Rabi. It records Sad's generous offer and Abd al-Rahman's request to be shown the market.
events.uncertainty: The report places the episode after the emigrants reached Madinah; no exact date is supplied.

events.title: The change of qiblah
events.summary: Al-Bara reports prayer toward Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months, followed by the change toward the Kaaba.
events.uncertainty: The narrator preserves a sixteen-or-seventeen-month uncertainty; the app keeps that uncertainty.

events.title: Supplication at Badr
events.summary: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet's earnest supplication at Badr and Abu Bakr's presence. Quran 3:123 explicitly names Badr.
events.uncertainty: The conventional year is a chronology aid. The report is cited for the supplication, not a complete battle narrative.

events.title: The archers at Uhud
events.summary: Al-Bara describes the instructions given to the archers under Abdullah ibn Jubayr and the consequences of leaving their position.
events.uncertainty: The conventional year is approximate in CE terms; details follow the named report.

events.title: A report on the retreat
events.summary: A second report from Al-Bara identifies the archers' commander and recalls the retreat during Uhud.
events.uncertainty: A separate report about the same battle, not another battle or an independently dated event.

events.title: Digging the trench
events.summary: Anas recalls the emigrants and helpers carrying earth while digging the trench, with hunger and difficult food supplies during the work.
events.uncertainty: The trench campaign is conventionally placed in 5 AH; the cited report describes the labor.

events.title: The account of the slander
events.summary: Aisha's extended report recounts the false accusation against her and the distress and eventual resolution that followed.
events.uncertainty: Its relation to some campaigns is debated. Placement in this band is approximate, not a claim of a precise year.

events.title: The journey to Hudaybiyah
events.summary: Al-Miswar and Marwan's account describes a journey intended for Umrah, negotiations with Quraysh, and the eventual agreement.
events.uncertainty: Conventional 6 AH placement. The linked report contains the detailed sequence.

events.title: The pledge beneath the tree
events.summary: Jabir recalls the group at Hudaybiyah and identifies the tree associated with the pledge. Quran 48:18 explicitly mentions the pledge beneath a tree.
events.uncertainty: Jabir gives a group count in this report. Other transmitted counts should not be silently harmonized.

events.title: Negotiating the written agreement
events.summary: The Hudaybiyah account records negotiations and the writing of treaty terms. Its difficult concessions form part of the report's sequence.
events.uncertainty: A detail of the same treaty episode, not a separate treaty.

events.title: The banner at Khaybar
events.summary: Sahl ibn Sad reports the announcement about the banner at Khaybar and its being given to Ali ibn Abi Talib.
events.uncertainty: The conventional year is shown; the linked report supports the banner episode.

events.title: A letter and questions from Heraclius
events.summary: Abu Sufyan's account describes Heraclius questioning him during the truce with Quraysh and a letter from the Prophet ﷺ.
events.uncertainty: The report explicitly situates the exchange during the truce. The CE placement is approximate.

events.title: The return for Umrah
events.summary: Al-Bara's report describes the agreement for a later visit to Makkah and a stay of three days under its terms.
events.uncertainty: The report links the visit to the agreement; its conventional chronology is 7 AH.

events.title: The approach to Makkah
events.summary: The report describes the approach during the year of the conquest and Abu Sufyan's encounter with the Muslim camp.
events.uncertainty: The year of the conquest is explicit in the report. CE conversion is approximate.

events.title: The Kaaba at the conquest
events.summary: Abdullah reports the removal of idols around the Kaaba when the Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah.
events.uncertainty: A detail of the conquest episode. No depictions of the Prophet are used.

events.title: Steadfastness at Hunayn
events.summary: Al-Bara reports that the Prophet ﷺ did not flee at Hunayn, while some people hurried away under the opposing archers' attack.
events.uncertainty: The conventional placement follows the conquest; the report supports this specific observation.

events.title: The expedition to Tabuk
events.summary: Kab ibn Malik's account describes his failure to join the expedition to Tabuk and the circumstances that followed.
events.uncertainty: Shown in the conventional 9 AH band. Read the complete report for its longer sequence.

events.title: Kab ibn Malik tells the truth
events.summary: Kab's account contrasts his truthful admission with the excuses he might have offered and recounts the eventual acceptance of repentance.
events.uncertainty: Part of the same report as Tabuk. Its relative sequence is more important here than an exact CE day.

events.title: Announcements during Abu Bakr's Hajj
events.summary: Abu Hurayra recalls being sent among the announcers at the Hajj led by Abu Bakr. The report also mentions Ali reciting Baraah.
events.uncertainty: Conventionally placed in 9 AH, before the Prophet's Farewell Hajj.

events.title: The Farewell Hajj
events.summary: Jabir's long report describes the announced pilgrimage in the tenth year, its journey, rites, and the address at Arafat.
events.uncertainty: The report explicitly identifies the tenth year in Madinah. Individual Gregorian date conversions are not asserted.

events.title: Conveying the message
events.summary: Abu Bakra reports an address on the Day of Nahr emphasizing the sanctity of life and property and conveying the message to those absent.
events.uncertainty: This report concerns the address at Mina; it is not silently merged with every other Farewell Hajj sermon.

events.title: The death of the Prophet ﷺ
events.summary: Aisha describes his final moments in her home. Another report records Abu Bakr addressing the community afterward and reciting Quran 3:144.
events.uncertainty: The year is conventional. The report supports the setting of the final moments; see the additional report for the community response.

cases.title: The first witness
cases.brief: Aisha's account takes us from Hira to a household conversation. Which sequence does the report support?

evidence.title: A place of seclusion
evidence.text: The account identifies Hira as the setting of the first encounter.

evidence.title: A trusted response
evidence.text: Khadija reassures him after hearing what happened.

evidence.title: A further conversation
evidence.text: Khadija takes the account to Waraqa ibn Nawfal.

answers: Hira, then Khadija's reassurance, then Waraqa.
Waraqa is present inside the cave.
The report gives an exact Gregorian day.
cases.conclusion: The report supports that sequence. It does not place Waraqa in Hira or provide an exact Gregorian date.
cases.hint: Follow the movement from the cave to the conversations afterward.

cases.title: The gathering at Safa
cases.brief: A gathering tests what the clans already know about the speaker. What can be established from Ibn Abbas's report?

evidence.title: A public summons
evidence.text: The Prophet ﷺ calls clans of Quraysh to Safa.

evidence.title: A question about trust
evidence.text: He asks whether they would believe a warning about approaching cavalry.

evidence.title: The response
evidence.text: Their reply acknowledges his truthfulness before the warning.

answers: The warning draws on an acknowledged record of truthfulness.
Every person present immediately accepts the message.
The report identifies the exact year of the gathering.
cases.conclusion: The report supports the acknowledgment of truthfulness. It does not say everyone accepted, and it supplies no exact CE year.
cases.hint: Separate what the audience says about trust from how every individual responds.

cases.title: After the rejection
cases.brief: Aisha asks about a particularly difficult experience. Which response is actually described?

evidence.title: The painful encounter
evidence.text: The report recalls rejection after approaching Ibn Abd Yalail.

evidence.title: An offered action
evidence.text: The Angel of the Mountains offers to bring the mountains down.

evidence.title: The response
evidence.text: The Prophet ﷺ declines and expresses hope for future descendants.

answers: He declines destruction and hopes for future worshippers.
The offered destruction is carried out immediately.
The report gives an exact date for an annual observance.
cases.conclusion: The stated response is hope for descendants, not the destruction offered. No exact anniversary is established by this report.
cases.hint: Distinguish the offer from the answer to it.

cases.title: Two in the cave
cases.brief: Abu Bakr describes a moment of danger during the migration. Which conclusion stays within this brief report?

evidence.title: The narrator
evidence.text: Abu Bakr recounts being in the cave with the Prophet ﷺ.

evidence.title: The concern
evidence.text: He fears that looking down would let the pursuers see them.

evidence.title: The reassurance
evidence.text: The reported reply reassures Abu Bakr about Allah's presence with them.

answers: The report records concern followed by reassurance.
This report describes a spider spinning a web.
This report names every person involved in the route.
cases.conclusion: The brief report establishes the concern and reassurance. It does not mention a spider's web or provide a full route list.
cases.hint: Avoid importing familiar details that are not present in the cited report.

cases.title: The pursuer's request
cases.brief: Suraqa pursues the travelers, but the encounter changes. What does he request before they continue?

evidence.title: A pursuit
evidence.text: Suraqa describes setting out after the travelers.

evidence.title: A changed situation
evidence.text: He recounts his horse stumbling and later sinking at the forelegs.

evidence.title: A written assurance
evidence.text: He asks for a statement of safety, which Amr ibn Fuhayra writes.

answers: A written assurance of safety.
A declaration that every future pursuer has already converted.
A complete map of the remaining journey.
cases.conclusion: The report specifies a written assurance of safety. The other conclusions add claims not made in these evidence cards.
cases.hint: Look for the request made after Suraqa approaches them.

cases.title: Where is the market?
cases.brief: A report about brotherhood includes a generous offer and an independent response. What does Abd al-Rahman ask for?

evidence.title: A bond
evidence.text: The account pairs Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf with Sad ibn al-Rabi.

evidence.title: An offer
evidence.text: Sad offers substantial help from his property.

evidence.title: The reply
evidence.text: Abd al-Rahman offers a blessing and asks to be shown the market.

answers: To be shown the market.
To be appointed ruler of the city.
To forbid anyone else from trading.
cases.conclusion: The report identifies the market request and subsequent trading. It does not support the claims about political appointment or excluding other traders.
cases.hint: Focus on the reply to Sad's offer.

cases.title: A direction changes
cases.brief: News reaches people who are already praying. Which detail should a careful reader preserve?

evidence.title: An earlier direction
evidence.text: Al-Bara describes prayer toward Jerusalem.

evidence.title: A narrated uncertainty
evidence.text: The duration is given as sixteen or seventeen months.

evidence.title: New information
evidence.text: A person who prayed with the Prophet ﷺ conveys the new direction to others.

answers: The report preserves uncertainty between sixteen and seventeen months.
The report gives exactly sixteen months with no uncertainty.
The report says every prayer before the change was invalid.
cases.conclusion: The narrator's sixteen-or-seventeen wording should remain visible. The other answers either erase uncertainty or introduce an unsupported conclusion.
cases.hint: A small uncertainty is evidence too; do not edit it out.

cases.title: The archers' instruction
cases.brief: The archers receive an instruction covering more than one possible outcome. What made leaving the position a problem?

evidence.title: A commander
evidence.text: Abdullah ibn Jubayr commands the archers in this report.

evidence.title: The instruction
evidence.text: They are told to remain until a message reaches them, even if either side appears to be winning.

evidence.title: A decision
evidence.text: Some leave after seeing an apparent victory and the prospect of spoils.

answers: The instruction explicitly covered an apparent victory as well as danger.
No instructions had been given about the position.
Every archer leaves and the report gives no exceptions.
cases.conclusion: The report makes the instruction explicit. An apparent victory did not cancel it. The absolute claim about every archer goes beyond these cards.
cases.hint: Read the condition about apparent victory, not just the condition about danger.

cases.title: The journey's purpose
cases.brief: Negotiators ask why the travelers have come. What purpose is stated in the Hudaybiyah account?

evidence.title: The journey
evidence.text: The account describes the approach to Hudaybiyah.

evidence.title: A stated purpose
evidence.text: The Prophet ﷺ explains that they have come for Umrah rather than to initiate fighting.

evidence.title: Negotiation
evidence.text: The narrative proceeds through messages and agreement terms.

answers: The stated purpose is Umrah, and negotiation follows.
The travelers state that they have come only for trade.
The report says no negotiation takes place.
cases.conclusion: The report explicitly distinguishes the intended Umrah from initiating battle. The existence of negotiation is part of the account.
cases.hint: Separate a stated purpose from later tensions during the journey.

cases.title: Who receives the banner?
cases.brief: An announcement makes people wonder who will receive a banner. Which identification is supported?

evidence.title: An announcement
evidence.text: The banner is to be given the next morning to a person described favorably.

evidence.title: Anticipation
evidence.text: Those present hope to receive it.

evidence.title: The outcome
evidence.text: The report names Ali ibn Abi Talib as its recipient.

answers: Ali ibn Abi Talib receives the banner in this report.
The recipient is chosen by a public vote described here.
The report never identifies who receives it.
cases.conclusion: The report identifies Ali. Anticipation among the companions is not evidence of a public vote.
cases.hint: Look for the recorded outcome rather than the expectations beforehand.

cases.title: Questions during a truce
cases.brief: Abu Sufyan describes an interview with Heraclius. What setting does the account explicitly preserve?

evidence.title: A narrator
evidence.text: Abu Sufyan reports the exchange to Ibn Abbas.

evidence.title: A period of truce
evidence.text: The account locates it during the truce between the Prophet ﷺ and Quraysh.

evidence.title: Questions and a letter
evidence.text: Heraclius asks questions, and the account includes the Prophet's letter.

answers: The interview occurs during the truce described by the narrator.
The report states that Heraclius publicly converts immediately.
The conversation happens before any prophetic mission begins.
cases.conclusion: The truce is explicit. The account should not be turned into an assertion of public conversion that it does not establish.
cases.hint: An interested response and a public conversion are different claims.

cases.title: News from a distant land
cases.brief: A death is announced, and a prayer follows. Which action is recorded in this report?

evidence.title: The news
evidence.text: Abu Hurayra recounts the announcement of al-Najashi's death.

evidence.title: The place
evidence.text: The group goes to the prayer ground and forms rows.

evidence.title: The prayer
evidence.text: The report records four takbirs in the funeral prayer.

answers: A funeral prayer in rows with four takbirs.
A journey by the entire group to attend a burial abroad.
An exact CE date is supplied in the report.
cases.conclusion: The report records the prayer and its four takbirs. It does not describe the group traveling abroad or give an exact Gregorian date.
cases.hint: Concentrate on what the group does after receiving the news.
